item.title: Resilient Transmission of Highly Structured Light via Active Convolved Illumination
item.description: arXiv:2611.17471v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Wave propagation through lossy and noisy systems as well as spatiotemporally dynamic random media often limits the complex information that can be reliably transmitted or retrieved. Progress in adaptive optics, wavefront shaping, machine learning, and wave propagation theories has significantly advanced physical and computational correction techniques. However, many approaches remain constrained by restrictive operating conditions, limiting their ability to meet growing application-specific demands, such as higher spatial resolution in imaging and greater data capacity in communications, particularly in highly dynamic environments. Recently, active convolved illumination (ACI) was proposed as a novel framework for preserving the spatial structure of optical modes during propagation through strongly distorting environments, such as atmospheric turbulence. ACI aims to bypass the prohibitive complexity of global distortion tracking by combining spectrally localized characterization with compensation using a correlated auxiliary source. Here, we provide a comprehensive review of ACI, detailing the formulation of correlation-injecting and auxiliary sources and the role of segmented reciprocal-space characterization and distortion compensation. We explore extensions in free-space optical communication and potential high-precision phase measurement, and numerically evaluate interferometric strategies for experimental implementation. This work highlights ACI as a potentially versatile framework for distortion-resilient light transmission, with broad interdisciplinary utility ranging from atmospheric physics and remote sensing to telecommunications, target tracking, and biomedical diagnosis, offering flexible deployment either as a standalone paradigm or hybridized with existing optical systems.
item.dc:creator: Anindya Ghoshroy, James Davis, Martin Wilkens, Sahin K. Ozdemir, Durdu O. Guney

item.title: 1.56 THz Full-Field Rydberg-Atom Imaging with 0.3 mm-scale Spatial Response
item.description: arXiv:2611.17558v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: THz imaging via Rydberg-atom up-conversion offers a powerful full-field modality with high sensitivity and rapid acquisition. However sub-millimeter imaging above 1 THz is still constrained by source power and beam-delivery loss. In this paper, we demonstrate a \(50~\mathrm{mm} \times 50~\mathrm{mm}\) full-field imaging at 1.56~THz by implementing the \(11P_{3/2} \rightarrow 10D_{5/2}\) transition of a cesium Rydberg-atom vapor. The measured spatial response FWHMs are \(0.314~\mathrm{mm}\) in horizontal and \(0.354~\mathrm{mm}\) in vertical for a \(0.5~\mathrm{mm}\) pinhole, alongside a sensitivity of \(31.7~\mathrm{fW}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1/2}/(6.5 \times 6.5)~\mu\mathrm{m}^{2}\), and a frame rate up to \(300~\mathrm{fps}\). Under matched illumination, relay, and image-processing conditions, mask imaging at 1.56 THz reproduces finer features and edges with substantially higher edge contrast, deeper intensity-trough separation in line profiles, and recovered detail that remains blurred or unresolved at 0.55 THz. Furthermore, preliminary imaging of a \(200~\mu\mathrm{m}\) tissue slice suggests morphological correspondence with H\&E histology histology, offered as a proof-of-concept for label-free tissue characterization. By validating the wavelength-dependent resolution scaling in Rydberg THz imaging, this work establishes frequency scaling as a general design principle for sub-millimeter Rydberg-THz imaging.
item.dc:creator: Xianzhe Li, Yibin Huang, Zhiwen Chen, Kaiqing Zhang, Haixiao Deng

item.title: Deep, label-free, volumetric lifetime microscopy via low-noise, single pulse sampling
item.description: arXiv:2611.17588v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fluorescence lifetime imaging (FLIM) provides label-free metabolic contrast, but conventional time-correlated single-photon counting requires thousands of excitation pulses per pixel to avoid pile-up distortion, limiting imaging speed and increasing motion artifacts and photodamage. Here, we develop single-pulse analog sampling that combines sub-photoelectron read noise with a jitter-immune, frequency-domain estimator for accurate lifetime measurement at low photon counts. Single low-flux traces achieve a photon economy of $F < 1.5$ at 100--150 detected photons, enabling accurate lifetime estimation from a single excitation pulse in label-free, volumetric samples. In in vivo zebrafish eyes, single-shot acquisition recovered the lifetime content of 20-pulse averaging at one-twentieth the exposure, resolving endogenous lipofuscin heterogeneity. In intact mouse kidney, scattering and reduced photon throughput impaired lifetime contrast; this was mitigated by lightweight denoisers that enabled label-free lifetime imaging to 200 micron depth at one pulse per pixel. These results establish single-shot FLIM as a route to deeper, faster, motion-tolerant, low-photodamage lifetime imaging.
item.dc:creator: Jack Tomkiewicz, Federico Presutti, Tade Marozsak, Jia Zhao, Hatoon Baazim, Hernandez Moura-Silva, Eliezer Calo, Sixian You

item.title: An Inverse-Designed Multilayer Selective Emitter for High-Efficiency Thermophotovoltaics
item.description: arXiv:2611.17675v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High thermophotovoltaic (TPV) conversion efficiencies have typically relied on photovoltaic cells that reflect sub-bandgap radiation back toward the emitter. Here, we numerically investigate an alternative approach in which spectral selectivity is engineered primarily on the emitter side. We optimize an emitter consisting of 16-layer aperiodic MgO/Si coating on tungsten, for coupling to a GaSb cell with an antireflection coating and an Au mirror. A detailed-balance framework incorporates polarization- and angle-resolved emissivity, multiple reflections, and Auger nonradiative recombination. At an emitter temperature of 1500 K, the optimized structure suppresses 97.1% of the incident-blackbody-equivalent sub-bandgap power at the source; a further 1.9% is returned to the emitter by the cell, leaving 1.0% absorbed parasitically in the cell. The resulting modeled radiative-to-electrical conversion efficiency reaches 47.0%, compared with 30.8% for a SiC emitter paired with the same cell, while maintaining a comparable maximum electrical power density. These findings indicate that emitter-side spectral engineering could substantially relax cell-side photon-recycling requirements and provide significant improvement in TPV conversion.
item.dc:creator: Md Anwar Hosen, Kavyashree Keremane, Bed Poudel, Linxiao Zhu

item.title: Uncertainty evaluation of length measurement by spectral domain interferometry with super-Gaussian windowing
item.description: arXiv:2611.17769v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this study, we evaluate the measurement uncertainty of spectral domain interferometry with super-Gaussian windowing, which has significant potential for interferometer-based dimensional calibration services owing to its simple configuration and nanometer-level precision. A super-luminescent diode (SLD) with a broadband spectrum was used as the light source for high-precision length measurement, and a frequency-calibrated spectrometer captured the spectral interference signal. The length measurement results were compared with a laser displacement interferometer. To evaluate the measurement uncertainty, numerical simulations were performed by considering the intensity-noise level of the CCD in the spectrometer and the frequency-axis uncertainty of the spectrometer. Through a comprehensive uncertainty analysis supported by numerical simulations, the combined standard uncertainty of the measured length was evaluated as sqrt((10 nm)^2 + (9.7x10^(-6)xL)^2). The resulting uncertainty budget provides a metrological basis for extending SLD-based SDI with super-Gaussian windowing toward interferometric dimensional calibration tasks over the millimeter-scale range.
item.dc:creator: Dae Hee Kim, Yoonkwon On, Sunghoon Eom, Chu-Shik Kang, Yoon-Soo Jang

item.title: Polarization Lifetime as a Design Axis for Task-Adaptive Photonic Reservoir Computing
item.description: arXiv:2611.17843v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Photonic time-delayed reservoir computing (TDRC) based on conventional Class B lasers is limited by fragile external cavity mode (ECM) locking dynamics. Here, we show that engineering the polarization lifetime (T$_2$) with the carrier lifetime ($T$) reshapes the topology and stability of TDRC. Comparing four laser classes (Class A, Class B, Class C$_A$, and Class C$_B$), a finite polarization lifetime acts as an intrinsic dynamic filter, dissolving discrete ECM chaos grids into continuous, phase-tolerant operational basins. Information processing capacity (IPC) decomposition further exposes distinct computational profiles: matched Class C$_A$ achieves the highest nonlinear capacity (16.28) and the highest total capacity (19.29), whereas Class A exhibits the highest linear capacity (4.70). A task-dependent reversal governs hardware design: Class A and Class C$_A$ achieve comparable, and the lowest, NRMSE on short-horizon Mackey--Glass prediction (0.0103 and 0.0105, within one standard deviation), while the time-scale-matched Class C$_A$ dominates the higher-dimensional Lorenz (0.0506) and the experimental Santa Fe (0.4251) tasks. Linear-IPC ranking matches Mackey-Glass accuracy; nonlinear-IPC ranking matches the Lorenz exactly and Santa Fe within the mask-to-mask uncertainty. Under realistic quantum noise, resilience is dictated mainly by $T$, not T$_2$: Class A retains the lowest NRMSE (0.47) even at spontaneous emission factor $\beta$ = $10^{-1}$, whereas the long-carrier Class B degrades (0.98). A residual T$_2$-mediated benefit of 20$\%$ persists in the slow-carrier Class C$_B$ (0.78 vs. 0.98). Time-scale engineering thus offers a nuanced design paradigm for optical computing, where optimal hardware is set by the task's time-scale hierarchy rather than a universal figure of merit.
item.dc:creator: Tao Wang, Kathy L\"udge

item.title: Antihelical Edge States in Photonic Metacrystals
item.description: arXiv:2611.17877v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Antihelical edge states represent a gapless form of boundary transport in which modes with opposite spin counterpropagate along a given boundary, while modes sharing the same spin propagate in the same direction on opposite boundaries. Here we show that such states arise naturally within a modified Kane-Mele framework realized in an electromagnetic-dual photonic metacrystal with staggered bianisotropy. Reversing the spin-dependent next-nearest-neighbor coupling on one sublattice reorganizes the bulk spectrum into a spin-polarized Dirac semimetal characterized by spin-dependent energy shifts of the Dirac cones rather than a bulk gap. This bulk reorganization generates tilted edge-mode dispersions in zigzag ribbons and gives rise to antihelical edge transport coexisting with bulk states. Full-wave simulations confirm the corresponding bulk and edge behaviors. Extending the analysis to finite geometries, simulations further reveal discrete corner-localized modes. A realistic design based on split-ring metaatoms is proposed to realize the required staggered bianisotropy and spin-dependent energy shifts of the Dirac cones. Furthermore, we show that the tensorial freedom of the bianisotropic constitutive relations enables continuous manipulation of the electromagnetic pseudospin basis while preserving the antihelical boundary transport. These results provide a practical route for engineering unconventional gapless boundary transport in photonic Dirac systems.
item.dc:creator: Ke-Yi Zeng, Zi-Xuan Gao, Zhou Zhou, Xiao-Dong Chen, Jian-Wen Dong

item.title: A Necessary and Sufficient Condition for Complete TE/TM Separability in Fully Anisotropic Waveguides
item.description: arXiv:2611.17888v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A necessary and sufficient condition is established for complete transverse-electric/transverse-magnetic (TE/TM) separability in waveguides homogeneously filled with a fully anisotropic and lossless medium. The permittivity and permeability tensors are Hermitian positive-definite and may contain nonzero transverse--longitudinal coupling terms. Complete TE/TM separation occurs if and only if the transverse permeability block is proportional to the transpose of the transverse permittivity block and the corresponding transverse--longitudinal coupling vectors satisfy the same proportionality relation after complex conjugation. The longitudinal constitutive entries remain independent apart from positive definiteness. The condition is derived directly from the source-free Maxwell equations, and independent analyses of the TE and TM modes lead to the same material relation. Since no boundary condition enters the derivation, the criterion is independent of the boundary type. Full-vector waveguide mode analyses using our in-house programs for perfect-electric-conductor and Bloch-periodic waveguides, with material tensors satisfying and violating the condition, agree with the theoretical results.
item.dc:creator: Wei Jiang, Jie Liu

item.title: Spectral dependence of Berry phase and topological bound states in the continuum in M\"obius resonators
item.description: arXiv:2611.17964v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The M\"obius strip and the bulk M\"obius resonator are of great interest to specialists in optics, acoustics, and quantum physics. Despite the apparent simplicity of the object and numerous publications, the M\"obius resonator, like a magic box, still holds many surprises. Here, we demonstrate experimentally, theoretically and with a simple illustrative example that in a "thin" M\"obius resonator with an odd number of twists, the longitudinal wavenumber is determined by the additional phase shift {\pi} (traditionally called the geometrical Berry phase) only if the total transverse index of the photonic mode is odd. For an even index, the Berry phase is zero. We also discovered "topological" quasi-bound states in the continuum in M\"obius resonators with a square cross-section; they differ from "ordinary" ones by the exchange of azimuthal indices of the interfering modes in the anti-crossing region. Finally, we demonstrate an example of resonant topology by determining the dependence of the Berry phase on the M\"obius resonator geometry based on the frequency difference between the eigenmodes of planar ring resonators and those of M\"obius resonators. The discovered effects significantly expand our knowledge of the topology of single resonators and promise new practical applications.
item.dc:creator: Mikhail E. Bochkarev, Timur Z. Seidov, Nikolay S. Solodovchenko, Kirill B. Samusev, Mikhail F. Limonov

item.title: Symmerty-Engineered Moire Metasurface for Multibeam Control
item.description: arXiv:2611.18032v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Moir\'e metasurfaces offer a versatile platform for wavefront engineering through the relative rotation of periodic structures. Despite extensive demonstrations of continuous beam steering, the physical mechanisms governing beam multiplicity remain poorly understood, hindering the systematic design of multibeam radiation states. Here, we establish a predictive framework for engineering beam multiplicity in reflective moir\'e metasurfaces based on the dominant Fourier coefficients of their constituent patterns. We reveal that the rotational symmetry of these Fourier components in reciprocal space fully determines the symmetry of the resulting moir\'e unit cell and, consequently, its radiation characteristics. By further incorporating their phase information, both beam multiplicity and steering trajectories can be accurately predicted. We demonstrate this approach using reflective moir\'e metasurfaces constructed from patterns with p6m, p3m1, and p4m plane-group symmetries, achieving one-, two-, three-, four-, and six-beam radiation states with continuously tunable steering trajectories. Beyond symmetry-based design, we identify two additional degrees of freedom for beam multiplicity control. Selecting different rotation centers reshapes the phase distributions of the dominant Fourier coefficients, enabling further manipulation of beam multiplicity and spatial arrangement, while varying the relative twist angle alters the pairing of Fourier components, inducing transitions between distinct beam multiplicities. These findings establish a systematic framework for versatile and reconfigurable multibeam wavefront engineering.
item.dc:creator: Yu Chen, Lan Ke, Shaojie Ma, Shuo Liu

item.title: Optical Representation Neural Networks Enabled by Weakly Supervised Learning
item.description: arXiv:2611.18045v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Diffractive optical neural networks (ONNs) show remarkable promise in high-speed and energy-efficient optical computing. However, most existing ONNs are optimized to reproduce predefined output intensity distributions, with the desired optical responses explicitly specified before training. Here, we introduce optical representation neural networks (ORNNs) enabled by coarse-grained weak supervision. Using handwritten Devanagari, Arabic, and English characters as three semantic groups, a modified contrastive objective encourages samples from the same script to cluster into similar optical representations. Remarkably, ORNNs improve the classification accuracy by approximately 9% over conventional supervised ONNs, while requiring only around 18% of the training steps to reach a stable test accuracy of 84.5%. These features can be selectively interpreted using corresponding semantic decoders. Building on this concept, we further realized semantic optical encryption with electronic neural network (ENN) decryption using experimentally acquired representations from a single-layer diffractive network fabricated by two-photon polymerization lithography (TPL). Here, we combine information from different scripts into a mixed optical ciphertext that is then first optically classified before being decrypted with a matched ENN. This work broadens the training paradigm of ONNs by coupling upstream optical representation learning with downstream task-specific decoding, opening new avenues for optical information processing.
item.dc:creator: Bochang Wu, Cheng-Feng Pan, Xuhao Luo, John You En Chan, Shutao Zhang, Zhenchao Liu, Hao Wang, Deepshikha Arora, Nur Qalishah Adanan, Ho Soon Yee, Lei Chen, Hongtao Wang, Wang Zhang, Cheng-Wei Qiu, Joel K. W. Yang

item.title: Commercial AlGaAs diodes provide simplified feedback for adaptive femtosecond pulse compression
item.description: arXiv:2611.18276v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Maintaining high peak power in ultrashort laser pulses is essential for efficient nonlinear interactions, particularly in multiphoton microscopy. Dispersion introduced by optical components broadens these pulses and degrades their peak power, thus motivating adaptive pulse compression guided by pulse-width-dependent feedback. However, the conventional second-harmonic generation feedback requires a nonlinear crystal, spectral filtering, and careful optical alignment. Here, we investigate commercially available AlGaAs laser and light-emitting diodes as alternative two-photon absorption feedback sensors. Their photocurrent exhibits a quadratic dependence on average optical power and inverse dependence on pulse duration, which is consistent with the analytical model predicting maximum response for the shortest, single-peaked pulse. Both devices generated a measurable photocurrent at sub-milliwatt average power levels and showed a weaker polarization dependence than second-harmonic-generation-based solution. All three feedback methods achieved comparable mean compressed pulse durations of 210-228 fs. These results demonstrate effective adaptive pulse compression with a substantially simpler feedback.
item.dc:creator: Patrycja H. Wysowska, Adrian Chlebowski, Lukasz A. Sterczewski, Jakub Bogus{\l}awski

item.title: Enhanced Hyperspectral Nano-FTIR Imaging by Neural-Network-Based Processing of Multiple Signal Harmonics
item.description: arXiv:2611.18387v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nano-FTIR spectroscopy combines infrared spectroscopy with nanometer-scale spatial resolution and enables hyperspectral nanoimaging. However, quantitative measurements typically rely on higher-harmonic near-field signals, which are largely background-free but suffer from low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Lower harmonics provide substantially higher SNR but contain significant background contributions that distort the near-field response and hinder quantitative analysis. Here, we introduce a cross-harmonic neural network (CHNN) that exploits the complementary information encoded in multiple harmonic channels to denoise third-harmonic hyperspectral data. Trained directly on experimental nano-FTIR datasets, the CHNN uses first- and second-harmonic spectra to improve the SNR of the third-harmonic response. Applied to a PMMA/PS polymer blend, it substantially reduces noise while preserving spectral features and nanoscale spatial contrast. Compared with conventional single-harmonic denoising using an autoencoder, the CHNN achieves superior noise suppression. These results demonstrate the potential of lower-harmonic signals for improving hyperspectral nano-FTIR imaging without increasing acquisition time.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Calvo-Barl\'es, Sergio G. Rodrigo, Luis Mart\'in-Moreno, Martin Schnell, Rainer Hillenbrand

item.title: Tunable Hybridization of Whispering Gallery Modes in High-Index Photonic Molecules
item.description: arXiv:2611.18426v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Photonic molecules formed by coupled dielectric microresonators provide a platform for controlling collective optical modes, yet the interplay between molecular topology, resonator detuning, and dielectric environment in determining their spectral response remains insufficiently quantified. Here, we systematically quantify the evolution of Whispering Gallery Mode (WGM) hybridization in high-index TiO$_2$ and perovskite coated TiO$_2$ microresonators with molecular topology, and establish the corresponding effective inter-cavity coupling using a combined numerical and analytical analysis. We further show that perovskite-shell incorporation provides a diameter and thickness-dependent modification of the effective coupling, producing a non-monotonic response rather than a uniform suppression of coupling. Despite the resulting closely spaced hybridized resonances in the high-index perovskite environment, the supermodes remain spectrally resolvable, with $Q$-factor of order \(10^3\) for representative modes. The observed spectral splitting is quantitatively related to the effective inter-cavity coupling strengths, revealing a non-monotonic coupling response to perovskite-shell incorporation that depends on resonator size and shell thickness. These results establish molecular topology and dielectric environment as distinct parameters for controlling WGM hybridization, inter-cavity coupling, and spectral response, providing a basis for the design of coupled resonator systems for applications in optical sensing, filtering, switching, and other resonant photonic devices.
item.dc:creator: Ayusmin Panda, Birabar Ranjit Kumar Nanda

item.title: In-plane diffusion, spurious drift and a physics-structured gap predictor for a free colloidal pair
item.description: arXiv:2611.17508v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: When the diffusivity of a Brownian particle depends on position, its mean displacement acquires a noise-induced (spurious) drift whose magnitude is set by the stochastic convention $\alpha$. We ask how much of this physics can be extracted from a pair of 1.95 $\mu$m polystyrene spheres released from blinking holographic optical tweezers at five bath temperatures between 2 and 40 $^\circ$C. The single-sphere diffusivity inside the pair stays between 0.093 and 0.098 $\mu$m$^2$ s$^{-1}$, whereas the Stokes-Einstein value for water rises from 0.126 to 0.361 $\mu$m$^2$ s$^{-1}$; an isolated sphere reproduces the deficit, which is therefore not a pair effect. From the measured gap-dependent diffusivities $D_\parallel(h)$ and $D_\perp(h)$ we build a Fokker-Planck predictor of the future gap and score it on held-out releases. It recovers the 90% width of the gap distribution up to 800 ms but cannot discriminate between $\alpha = 0$, $1/2$ and $1$, because the $\alpha$-dependent mean shift is an order of magnitude smaller than that width. The ensemble spurious drift is consistent with zero at both ends of the temperature range, and the regression for $\alpha$ never exceeds $R^2 = 0.22$. We therefore present a planar methods baseline and identify the measurements required to resolve $\alpha$.
item.dc:creator: Juan Pablo Staforelli Vivanco, Cristobal Augusto Vald\'es Cruces

item.title: Sign-switchable and tunable macroscopic curvature of liquid jets by microscopic laser-induced cavitation
item.description: arXiv:2611.17860v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Localized forcing of liquid jets can trigger Rayleigh-Plateau breakup at low perturbation amplitudes or explosive fragmentation at high amplitudes, while controlled bending in the intermediate regime has remained unexplored. We show that femtosecond-laser-induced cavitation, seeded at the interface of a 100 micrometre-diameter water jet, produces a selectable curvature in 0.4-1 mm long segments. Cavitation rupturing at the liquid-air interface drives fast outward jetting and induces a slower recoil on the opposite boundary, which evolves on the capillary-inertial timescale and results in curving of the liquid segment. The curvature is governed by three laser parameters. Off-axis laser illumination on the jet shifts the refractive caustics and redistributes energy deposition between the front and rear interfaces. The resulting recoil imbalance determines the curvature sign, with a straight configuration in the balanced case. Laser energy offers additional control over the recoil impulse via plasma defocusing and nonlinear absorption in the liquid jet, where the response is bounded by axisymmetric deformation at low energy and explosive vaporization at high energy. Repetition rate sets the spacing between successive cavitation events and hence the length of the bent segment. Curvature extends across the segment for lengths of 6-10 jet diameters; shorter segments undergo Rayleigh-Plateau breakup, whereas longer ones bend mainly near their retracting ends. Our results offer a platform for optofluidic control of switchable and tunable macroscopic curvature in flowing liquid jets.
item.dc:creator: Sourabh Singh, S. Sree Harsha, Prashant Kumar Singh

item.title: A Concise Introduction to Quantum Electromagnetics
item.description: arXiv:2611.17988v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This book introduces quantum electromagnetics to readers trained in classical electromagnetics, without assuming a systematic background in quantum mechanics. The central question is when classical descriptions suffice, and when the quantum states of matter or the field must be retained explicitly. Starting from familiar electromagnetic modes and material response, the discussion develops atomic dynamics, field quantization, and the interaction of quantized fields with quantum matter. Particular attention is given to how mode profiles, Green functions, and scattering matrices obtained from classical electromagnetic calculations enter quantum models. Atomic coherence, photon statistics, spontaneous emission, and cavity coupling are developed through derivations that identify the physical assumptions and limits of each description. Examples drawn from atomic clocks, Rydberg-atom receivers, and single-photon devices connect these concepts to excitation, propagation, and measurement in practical systems. Loss and noise are included in relating internal dynamics to measured signals and correlations. The final discussion examines how sensitivity and claims of quantum advantage depend on bandwidth, measurement resources, and the classical reference used for comparison. The aim is to help readers choose an appropriate model, carry out the calculation, and understand what its predictions mean for an electromagnetic measurement.
item.dc:creator: Wei E. I. Sha

item.title: Linear-optical generation of approximate higher-component cat states
item.description: arXiv:2611.18065v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a method for generating higher-component cat states by interfering two $N$-component cat states on a half beam splitter and measuring one output with a photon-number-resolving detector. The Fock components of the conditional output are restricted to a single residue class modulo $2N$. For $N=3$, an ideal six-component cat state can be generated exactly, while for arbitrary $N$, the conditional output approaches an ideal $2N$-component cat state for sufficiently large input amplitudes.
item.dc:creator: Shohei Kiryu, Masahiro Takeoka

item.title: Fundamental and multihumped multimode solitons in fibers : new families of solitons and their properties
item.description: arXiv:2611.18159v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We describe multimode solitons made of purely spatial modes using the mathematical formalism developed for the elliptical polarization soliton, and we extend this formalism to solitons made of more than two modes. The main difference with the polarization mode case is the asymmetry in the nonlinear coefficients. Strictly speaking, these objects are solitary waves, whose modal temporal profiles remain invariant owing to the incoherent nonlinear interaction between modes. The approach consists of finding the trajectories of a unit-mass ball in an analogous potential, which correspond to stationary solutions of our set of nonlinear coupled equations. Our analysis reveals a rich variety of multimode solitons with more complex temporal profiles, so-called multihumped multimode solitons. These are new and highly complex nonlinear objects. While fundamental multimode solitons are stable against noise and symmetry breaking, the stability of multihumped multimode solitons depends on their position in the parameter space. The fission of multihumped solitons yields several less complex multihumped solitons, together with fundamental multimode solitons. For the latter, Raman nonlinearity can induce a net energy transfer between modes with different group velocities, whereas self-steepening only modifies the overall velocity of the solitary wave.
item.dc:creator: Julien Dechanxhe, Pascal Kockaert, Spencer W. Jolly

item.title: Number fluctuations and particle loss in Dicke superradiance
item.description: arXiv:2611.18413v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Dicke superradiance, the collective spontaneous emission of identical quantum emitters into a common reservoir, produces a burst with a characteristic delay $t_{\mathrm{SR}}$ and a peak intensity that scales quadratically with the emitter number $N$. This strong dependence makes the burst sensitive to how many emitters actually participate. In experiments, however, this number is rarely fixed: it fluctuates between preparations and decreases during emission through atom loss. Here we extend the analytical treatment of superradiance to variable emitter numbers using the Schwinger-boson mapping of the collective spin onto two bosonic modes. In this formulation, collective decay annihilates an atom in the excited-state mode and creates one in the ground-state mode. We find that number fluctuations enhance emission and that the ensemble-averaged emission trace encodes the initial number distribution. We show how to reconstruct second-order correlations from photon counting with finite detection efficiency and temporal resolution, even when the full distribution cannot be resolved. For atom loss at rate $r$, we derive exact results for the population dynamics and show that the peak intensity scaling is governed by the single scaling variable $g_{\mathrm{r}}=r t_{\mathrm{SR}}$. The peak remains quadratic in $N$ for $g_{\mathrm{r}}<1$, follows logarithmically corrected subquadratic power laws for $g_{\mathrm{r}}>1$, and crosses over to linear scaling under strong loss with $g_{\mathrm{r}}\gg1$.
item.dc:creator: Christian Niehof, Nico S. Bassler, Claudiu Genes

item.title: Topological phase diagram of an extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model with negative coupling
item.description: arXiv:2611.18456v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recently, an extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model with three atoms per unit cell has been experimentally realized in perovskite exciton-polariton micropillars. A distinctive feature of this system is that the second and third bands undergo a topological transition through a band crossing at the wave vector $k=0$, associated with a negative coupling. In this work, we analytically determine the phase diagram of the model as a function of the on-site energy splitting and the ratio of intercell to intracell hopping amplitudes. We identify seven regions in this lane, with four distinct topological phases, characterized by different Zak phases of the three bands. Our results provide a useful theoretical framework for interpreting existing experiments and serve as a guide for future experimental investigations of this system.
item.dc:creator: P. A. Grizzi, P. Roura-Bas, A. A. Aligia

item.title: Symmetry-Engineered Magnetic Dipole Emission in Plasmonic Core-Satellite Resonators
item.description: arXiv:2604.07140v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Magnetic dipole (MD) transitions are intrinsically weak and highly sensitive to emitter orientation and position, making their controlled enhancement at optical frequencies particularly challenging. Here we show that structural symmetry provides a powerful route to robust magnetic light-matter interactions. We systematically investigate plasmonic core-satellite resonators composed of N metallic nanoparticles arranged on a dielectric core. We evaluate their performance using a unified figure of merit that accounts for magnetic Purcell enhancement, electric dipole suppression, quantum efficiency, and robustness to emitter orientation and fabrication tolerances. We find that the optimal structures correspond to the highest-symmetry geometries, which naturally produce spatially homogeneous and orientation-independent magnetic Purcell enhancement. In particular, the dodecapod configuration yields strong magnetic emission with Purcell factors approaching 590, good radiative efficiency, and suppressed electric dipole contributions. Quasinormal-mode and complex mode-volume analysis reveal that symmetry enforces uniform magnetic modal confinement within the core, explaining both the enhancement and its robustness. These results establish symmetry as a guiding principle for designing nanophotonic resonators with controlled multipolar light-matter interactions and provide a practical route toward bright and selective magnetic dipole emitters.
item.dc:creator: Joshua Davis, S\'ebastien Bidault, Mathieu Mivelle, Mona Tr\'eguer-Delapierre, Alexandre Baron

item.title: Symmetry-breaking and hysteretic transitions in an actively coupled optical trimerhrough chaotic hysteresis in a non-Hermitian optical trimer
item.description: arXiv:2605.29844v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the nonlinear dynamics of a non-Hermitian optical trimer consisting of three lossy waveguides with complex-valued coupling. Building on our previous analysis of its global dynamics, we adopt a site-resolved approach to elucidate the bifurcation structure and the organization of oscillatory states across the individual waveguides. We identify a hysteretic transition from reflection-asymmetric periodic states to periodic states exhibiting a combined reflection-translation symmetry. This transition involves a double-loop hysteretic regime characterized by the coexistence of multiple attractors. Analysis of the spatial intensity profiles and their Fourier spectra reveals distinct oscillatory behavior among the waveguides. In particular, in the regime with combined reflection-translation symmetry, the central waveguide exhibits a dominant spatial wavenumber approximately twice that of the edge waveguides. We further identify a third dynamical regime emerging through a pitchfork bifurcation of limit cycles, which breaks the combined reflection--translation relation and gives rise to two reflection-related periodic solutions. Despite this transition, the 2:1 relation between the dominant spatial wavenumbers of the central and edge waveguides persists. These results demonstrate how nonlinear interactions, complex coupling, and dissipation shape multistability, chaotic dynamics, bifurcations, and site-dependent oscillations in a minimal non-Hermitian photonic system.
item.dc:creator: Johanne Hizanidis, Konstantinos G. Makris

item.title: Exceptional Points of Temporal Coherent Perfect Absorption in the Momentum Bandgap of a Photonic Time Crystal
item.description: arXiv:2607.14912v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We report exceptional points (EPs) of temporal coherent perfect absorption (CPA) in the momentum bandgap of a photonic time crystal. Confinement of the photonic time crystal in a cavity with finite length gives rise to discrete momentum modes, and therefore enables coherent matching of a single light source to a selected decaying Floquet mode. Meanwhile, excitation of the corresponding growing Floquet mode is suppressed by destructive self-interference. Two CPA branches coalesce at second-order EPs, leading to a quartic absorption lineshape and enhanced robustness against momentum detuning. Phase control further reveals the nontrivial topology of the CPA manifold, in which CPA at the wavevector of maximum Floquet rate exhibits a double phase winding around a third-order EP. Compared to conventional CPA EPs that rely on material absorption, temporal CPA EPs transfer the source energy to the external modulation, providing the basis for high energy efficiency and suppressed local heating. These results indicate the great potential of photonic time crystals for coherent control of light in integrated nanophotonic devices.
item.dc:creator: Yuhang Li, Zilong Bao, Yu Zhuang, Jingwen Cui, Junda Wang, Zhanchun Zuo, Xiulai Xu, Chenjiang Qian

item.title: Boundary-sensitive non-Hermiticity of the Floquet Hamiltonian: Spectral transition and scale-free localization
item.description: arXiv:2603.22746v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We report a novel mechanism of boundary-sensitive PT symmetry breaking in one-dimensional Floquet systems. By designing a time-periodic driving protocol, we realize a Floquet Hamiltonian that is Hermitian under periodic boundary conditions yet acquires non-Hermitian boundary terms under open boundary conditions due to the non-commutativity of driving Hamiltonians. We show that boundary-induced PT breaking can occur when the boundary term couples Bloch modes that become degenerate after their quasienergy bands cross the frequency Brillouin zone boundary. For a single band, this requires the quasienergy bandwidth to span the entire frequency Brillouin zone, whereas in multi-band systems the relevant threshold is determined by the bands that can be coupled by the boundary terms. In the PT-broken phase, the eigenstates exhibit scale-free localization arising from the system-size scaling of the induced non-Hermitian terms. The associated wave-packet accumulation near the boundaries provides a dynamical signature of the transition. Finally, we present a general framework for constructing single- and multiband models exhibiting this phenomenon.
item.dc:creator: Bo Li, He-Ran Wang, Fei Song

item.title: Efficient photon-pair emission from a nanostructured resonator and its theoretical description
item.description: arXiv:2603.24351v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) in subwavelength nanostructures is a promising source of quantum light, owing to its multifunctionality and ability to generate complex quantum states. Nevertheless, the mechanisms governing photon-pair generation in such systems remain only partially understood. In particular, experimental investigations of key emission properties in individual resonators, such as directionality and spectral distribution, are still lacking, and predictive theoretical frameworks have not yet been experimentally validated. Here, we report the first measurement of the directional and spectral distributions of photon pairs generated via SPDC in a nanostructured resonator. Both distributions exhibit resonant behaviour, which we describe using an extended quasi-normal-mode theory. This comparison is enabled by photon-pair count rates of up to 0.45 Hz/mW -- to our knowledge, the highest reported for a nanostructured resonator. Our results provide new physical insight into nanoscale SPDC and represent an important step toward designing of efficient miniaturized quantum light sources.
item.dc:creator: Michael Poloczek, Alberto Paniate, Attilio Zilli, Vitaliy Sultanov, Yigong Luan, Tom\`as Santiago-Cruz, Luca Carletti, Marco Finazzi, Marco Genovese, Ivano Ruo-Berchera, Marzia Ferrera, Andrea Toma, Francesco Monticone, Michele Celebrano, Maria Chekhova

item.title: Puiseux series about exceptional singularities dictated by symmetry-allowed Hessenberg forms of perturbation matrices
item.description: arXiv:2603.25603v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a systematic framework for determining the nature of exceptional points of $n^{\rm th}$ order (EP$_n$s) in non-Hermitian (NH) systems, represented by complex square matrices. By expressing symmetry-preserving perturbations ($\propto \epsilon$) in the Jordan-normal basis of the defective matrix at an EP$_n$, we show that the upper-$\ell$ Hessenberg structure of the perturbation matrix directly dictates the leading-order eigenvalue- and eigenvector-splitting to be $\propto \epsilon^{1/\ell}$, when expanded in a Puiseux series. Applying this to three-band NH models invariant under parity (P), charge-conjugation (C), or parity-time-reversal (PT), we find that EP$_3$s in P- and C-symmetric systems are restricted to at most $\sim \epsilon^{1/2}$ branch points, while PT-symmetric systems generically support EP$_3$s with the strongest possible singularities (viz. $\sim \epsilon^{1/3}$). We illustrate these results with concrete three-dimensional models in which exceptional curves and surfaces emerge. We further show that fine-tuned perturbations can suppress the leading-order branch point to a less-singular splitting, which have implications for designing direction-dependent EP-based sensors. The appendix extends the analysis to four-band P- and C-symmetric models, establishing the existence of EP$_4$s with $\sim \epsilon^{1/4}$ and $\sim \epsilon^{1/2}$ singularities, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Ipsita Mandal

item.title: Dual-Pilot-Assisted Frequency and Phase Recovery in Experimental CV-QKD
item.description: arXiv:2608.07277v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) offers high secret-key rates and compatibility with optical communication infrastructure. Locally generated local oscillator (LLO) architectures reduce security vulnerabilities associated with transmitting a strong optical reference, but independent lasers introduce frequency offsets and phase fluctuations that require accurate compensation. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a Gaussian-modulated LLO CV-QKD system over 12 km of optical fiber using two frequency-multiplexed pilot tones and RF-heterodyne detection with independent lasers. The proposed digital signal processing (DSP) architecture integrates CAZAC-based frame synchronization, global and subframe-wise carrier-frequency-offset estimation, and coherent dual-pilot phase recovery. We analyze 120 experimental frames, each containing approximately $10^6$ coherent states, and directly compare single-pilot and dual-pilot processing using identical acquisitions. The dual-pilot DSP chain achieves an average input-referred excess noise of $15.56 \pm 7.61$ mSNU, representing reductions of 28.1% and 17.4% relative to pilots 1 and 2, respectively. Under a trusted-receiver security model, the system achieves average modeled secret-key rates of $14.98 \pm 4.18$ Mbit/s in the asymptotic regime and $8.17 \pm 2.53$ Mbit/s using conservative finite-size parameter-estimation bounds. These results demonstrate the experimental benefits of jointly exploiting two pilot references for frequency and phase recovery in LLO CV-QKD systems, supporting their development for metropolitan quantum communication networks.
item.dc:creator: Christiano M. S. Nascimento, Artur A. Matoso, Gustavo C. Amaral, Guilherme P. Tempor\~ao

item.title: Heuristic Lookahead Distillation Protocol Search
item.description: arXiv:2608.13644v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Bipartite qubit entanglement distillation is the process of converting noisy ebits into pure ebits using only local operations and classical communication. This is a core operation for quantum repeaters, enabling such crucial tasks as long-distance quantum communication and distributed quantum computing. In this work, we introduce a method for searching for entanglement distillation protocols and, using this technique, distil qubit Werner states at a higher rate than could be achieved using previously discovered protocols. In particular, we demonstrate the advantage of our new distillation strategy by improving the best known lower bound for the two-way-assisted quantum capacity of the qubit depolarising channel across a wide range of channel parameters, making progress in one of the long-standing problems of quantum information theory.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Barber, Stefano Pirandola

item.title: Improved lower bound for the two-way-assisted quantum capacity of the bosonic thermal-loss channel
item.description: arXiv:2609.27792v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The bosonic thermal-loss channel is a fundamental model for quantum communication. This Gaussian channel models the transmission of bosonic systems subject to both loss and thermal noise. It describes many practical systems, including optical fibres, waveguides and free-space links, where background thermal noise is significant. Determining the channel's two-way-assisted quantum capacity, the maximum rate at which quantum information can be transmitted reliably through the channel with two-way classical assistance, remains an open problem. Here, we improve upon the best known lower bound for this capacity for a wide range of channel parameters. We achieve this by combining an improved qubit-bosonic distribution technique with a recently introduced technique for discovering entanglement distillation protocols.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Barber, Stefano Pirandola
